summary: A member that leaves records how far it wrote in the messages shard, so its envelopes up to there stay valid after it leaves or rejoins, and a keyed member's first shard message no longer fails (db break-up step 4c-1, part B)

replay.detail: A member that leaves, and has written to the messages shard, first writes a new fleet.shard-bounds claim, signed by its own key, with its last shard sequence (shard_high_water). fleet.member-left and fleet.member-admitted are unchanged. In a real install nothing writes the shard yet (only the test route does), so no leave writes one today. A shard store no longer mints principal keys or writes principal.key-granted: principal facts live in the graph, and a shard envelope is signed by the member key.

schema.detail: New claim kind fleet.shard-bounds (subject host; member_key, shard_high_water). The graph gains two triggers that keep the fleet membership cache current when one is admitted. No table or user_version change.

rules.detail: A shard envelope is admitted by its writer's key at its sequence. The writer's latest key, while it has not ended, counts at every sequence. A key that left counts at or below the high-water its own signed fleet.shard-bounds names, and at no sequence without one. Bounds count only at a writer sequence at or below the key's fleet.member-left, so bounds the key signs after it left raise nothing. A key superseded without a leave never counts, nor does a removed key. When the graph's membership changes (a bounds claim admitted after the envelopes it decides), the shard judges the envelopes it held again, at startup after the graph's own pass and at its next exchange, even one that brings nothing new. Because an envelope's identity includes its hash, a member that rejoins under the same name writes envelopes distinct from its old key's, and both stay valid. Known limit: a member reset without a leave, so that its old key is lost, strands that key's envelopes that no peer holds yet, as before.

compatibility.detail: An older build does not know fleet.shard-bounds, so it holds the claim as an unknown claim kind, one per leave attempt, and admits it when it upgrades; its shard then admits the leaver's envelopes at or below the bound at once, without waiting for new stream items. Until then it keeps its stricter rule, the writer's latest unended key only, so it fences a leaver's envelopes rather than admitting them. It never admits more than this build. No fleet barrier.

recovery.detail: Rolling back keeps the bounds claims in the graph, held by the older build until it upgrades again. The older build fences a leaver's shard envelopes by its stricter rule.
